The vulnerability, dubbed Upload2Shell and tracked as CVE-2026-125396, affects upstream Ghostscript releases before 10.08.0. findings.summary: ## Summary When validating an incoming block header, `HeaderSigVerifier.verifyConsensusSize` counts *every* set bit in `PubKeysBitmap` — including bits that correspond to no validator (the padding bits of the final byte, which exist whenever the consensus group size is not a multiple of 8). The subsequent BLS aggregate-signature verification (`blsMultiSigner.Verify`) only checks signature validity for real validator indices and silently ignores those padding bits.

findings.summary: ### Summary The JLine3 built-in `less` pager compiles user-supplied search patterns directly as Java regular expressions with no sanitization, timeout, or backtracking bound. A malicious pattern such as `(a+)+b` can trigger catastrophic backtracking and hang the session thread at 100% CPU. In deployments that expose `less` over Telnet or SSH, this becomes a denial-of-service issue for the affected session and can be used to exhaust a bounded session pool.
findings.title: jline3 leads to ReDoS in Built-in Less Viewer Search

findings.summary: A critical flaw in simple-git, a popular Node.js library for running Git commands, can let attackers run their own commands on a server. The issue is tracked as CVE-2026-134815. It affects apps that pass untrusted input into Git arguments. The National Vulnerability Database says simple-git versions before 4.1.0 contain an argument injection weakness, listed as CWE-88. In plain terms, the library does not properly separate user-supplied text from the options it sends to Git.

findings.summary: Hackers are breaking into Check Point Security Management Servers. These servers hold the rules that decide what traffic a company’s firewalls allow or block. A new campaign has already hit at least 22 organizations worldwide, and the attacker still has access to many of them. Check Point management servers are a high-value target because they work like a control room for firewalls. Whoever controls one can read the firewall settings, copy stored credentials, and change the security policy.

findings.summary: A new Linux backdoor called ZQAgent is giving attackers a long-term foothold on compromised servers. It can run commands, move through folders, read files and open network tunnels. It also hides itself to look like a normal system process. The malware was dropped by ARTEX, an AI-driven hacking framework. Most ARTEX intrusions are quick smash-and-grab jobs that steal passwords and leave. This case is different, because the operator wanted to stay inside the network for a long time.

findings.summary: ### Impact `verify_envelope_bsp()` derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted `wsse:BinarySecurityToken`, validated **only** that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning.

findings.summary: A Windows user searching for a screenshot tool was redirected to a fake download site and given a Microsoft-signed installer. But instead of installing the Snipping Tool, the installer led to a Microsoft Store app called Setup Assistant. That app opened a backdoor and delivered Vinci RAT, a remote access trojan that can run commands, place files on an infected PC, and launch additional malware. The case stands out because the fake download page did not merely imitate the Microsoft Store.
findings.title: Vinci RAT Linked to Microsoft Store Raises Risk of Hackers Remotely Controlling Windows PCs

findings.summary: Remus Stealer is silently installing a fake Google Sheets extension in Google Chrome to steal Gmail messages from signed-in users. The extension runs in the background on compromised Windows computers, reading new emails and sending their contents to an attacker-controlled server. Despite claims by the malware’s developers, researchers found no evidence that the feature exploits a Gmail zero-day. It relies on the victim already being signed in.
findings.title: Remus Stealer Silently Installs Fake Google Sheets Extension to Steal Gmail Messages

The November 25 PAN-OS security bulletin lists fixes across five software branches.

Dell disclosed the issue on November 19, 2026, and assigned it a CVSS score of 9.9 out of 10.

findings.summary: A Windows installer named HardwareInfo.msi delivers browser-stealing malware that uses signed Windows components and a signed Firefox add-on to look less suspicious. The toolkit targets saved passwords, session cookies, and other browser data. Its code also points to a more serious goal: giving a remote operator control of a hidden browser that is already signed in to the victim’s accounts.
findings.title: Hackers Abuse Microsoft and Mozilla Trusted Signing to Deploy Malware That Steals Browser Passwords

findings.summary: A fake Minecraft mod named Farmutils-Loader.jar steals players’ active Minecraft session tokens and delivers a Python infostealer on Windows. The Java archive poses as a library for Fabric, a popular Minecraft mod loader. When the game loads it, the file reads the player’s session from memory, then starts a background process that downloads the next stage inside what appears to be an ordinary PNG image. Launching Minecraft is not the only way to trigger the malware.
findings.title: Fake Minecraft Mod Steals Players’ Session Tokens and Deploys Python Infostealer

findings.summary: An Iran-linked cyberespionage group called Volant Manticore used a fake résumé to target a Cyprus-based airline and later turned to healthcare-themed phishing in Saudi Arabia. Both campaigns delivered KuboShell, a newly documented Windows backdoor that lets operators run commands on infected computers. The group also targeted telecommunications companies and critical infrastructure in Cyprus, its main focus before the Saudi campaign. The airline lure surfaced in July 2026.
findings.title: Iran-Linked Volant Manticore Hackers Target Airlines and Hospitals With New KuboShell Backdoor

findings.summary: SolarWinds released Serv-U 2026.4 on November 24, 2026, fixing 18 vulnerabilities, including nine critical flaws, two of which could grant attackers root access on Linux servers, while the risk is lower on Windows. However, the same update also fixes a high-severity command injection flaw that affects only Windows installations. The Serv-U 2026.4 release notes identify CVE-2026-123172 and CVE-2026-123168 as the two flaws that could grant Linux root privileges.

Endpoint security stopped that part of the attack within roughly 90 seconds. A separate, closely related sample contained Gh0stRAT malware capable of logging keystrokes, capturing screens, and accessing a PC’s webcam and microphone.

findings.summary: The Node.js project released a version 27.0.0-alpha.0.2.0 on November 26, 2026, bringing security fixes for reused HTTP connections and new controls for TLS 1.2 renegotiation. The official release notes also list changes to HTTP/2 memory limits and HTTPS connection pooling. The alpha does not remove TLS 1.2 or turn off renegotiation by default. Instead, it gives developers a way to disable renegotiation now and test which services still depend on it.
findings.title: Node.js 27 Alpha Adds HTTP Security Protections and Deprecates TLS 1.2 Renegotiation

findings.summary: Hackers planted PolinRider malware in 375 GitHub repositories, hiding a Python loader in ordinary-looking project files. The loader retrieves JavaScript stored in an Ethereum transaction and runs it through Node.js. In some projects, running tests is enough to trigger the loader. In others, it can run when the application starts and imports the planted module. The affected public repositories belonged to 260 accounts, and 370 had received a push in November 2026.
findings.title: Hackers Hide PolinRider Malware in 375 GitHub Repositories to Execute Malicious Code

Defender recorded the outbound connection, data preparation and attempts to discover accounts.

findings.summary: A malicious website could expose a Tor Browser user’s public IP address with a single click, according to research published by security firm Calif on November 26, 2026. Researcher Carlos Roque demonstrated the attack against Tor Browser 15.0.22 on Linux with default settings. The Tor Project had already shipped the fix in Tor Browser 15.0.23 on September 15, more than two months before the research became public. The click happened after the user opened the malicious page.

findings.summary: The UK’s Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) took a wide range of its online services offline on November 27, 2026, after identifying what it calls a cyber incident affecting its systems . Claimants have since been unable to sign in to Universal Credit accounts, apply for Personal Independence Payment (PIP) or the State Pension online, or use the Tell Us Once service to report a death. The DWP cyber incident has not touched scheduled payments.

findings.summary: Fake Facebook ads offering free animated Windows wallpapers are spreading SYS010, an information stealer that targets Meta Business accounts and webmail. The download delivers a working wallpaper app, but it also runs malware in the background. On selected computers, the malware forces browsers to install extensions that can steal session cookies and collect Facebook advertising data. The Chrome variant can also read Gmail and Outlook messages.

findings.summary: A critical Linux kernel flaw called NFS2ROOT could let an attacker take full control of an unpatched Network File System (NFS) server without logging in. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-99362 , affects the Linux kernel’s NFS server when NFSv4.1 or NFSv4.2 is enabled and an attacker can reach TCP port 2049. The affected code dates back to Linux 3.16, released in 2014. OpenSec Intelligence gave the flaw a severity score of 9.8 out of 10 and showed what it could do in a controlled test.
findings.title: 12-Year-Old NFS2ROOT Linux Flaw Let Hackers Take Full Control of Servers Without a Password
